note: Descriptive statistics of saved predictions. No model, threshold or feature was fitted or chosen with these numbers.

definitions.onset: First hour with observed PM2.5 >= 35 after at least 6 consecutive observed hours below 35, per receptor node.
definitions.model_lead_h: Onset time minus the issue time of the earliest forecast that predicts level >= 2 for the onset hour or later. Only forecasts whose valid time is at or after the onset count, so the maximum is 3. Negative means the alert came after the onset. 'missed' means no such forecast before the episode ended (or within 12 h of the onset, whichever is earlier).
definitions.index_lag_h: Hours after the onset until the 24 h running mean of observed PM2.5 first reaches 35 (needs 18 observed hours). 'never' means it did not within 48 h. Onsets where the running mean was already at or above 35 one hour earlier are counted separately as index_already_elevated and left out of the comparison.
definitions.advantage_h: model_lead_h plus index_lag_h, for onsets where both exist.
definitions.alert_precision: Share of forecast alert onsets (a predicted level >= 2 after 6 predicted hours below 2) with an observed high-risk hour between one hour before and three hours after the predicted hour.
definitions.index_note: The running mean stands in for an index built on a daily average. It uses the same CAMS series and the project's own 35 µg/m³ boundary. It is not the official Malaysian API.
definitions.calibration: Ten equal-width bins of the M6 cumulative probability P(level >= k). ECE is the sample-weighted mean absolute gap between mean predicted probability and observed frequency.
definitions.error: M5 concentration forecast minus realised concentration, µg/m³. Negative means the forecast was too low.
definitions.trend: rising: realised concentration exceeds current PM2.5 by more than 10; falling: is lower by more than 10; otherwise steady.
